title: Bridging the Gap Between Research and Practice in Literacy Instruction
author: Geoghegan, Brittany
summary: 54% of U.S. adults read below a sixth-grade level; 64% of fourth graders don't read proficiently. Teacher training programs still teach discredited methods. Teachers themselves trained in whole language can't apply phonics because they never learned it. Quality professional development grounded in science-based instruction is critical immediately. Organizations like Teach Like a Champion, UFLI, and Freedom In Education researchED conferences are filling the gap.
points: Most colleges of education still teach discredited balanced literacy and whole language methods.
Newer teachers trained in these flawed methods can't intuitively know what works; they need explicit evidence-based training.
Quality PD grounded in research and demonstrating real classroom application makes immediate difference.
Teachers cannot wait for colleges to reform; grassroots PD initiatives must bridge the gap now.
Organizations offering research-backed PD (Teach Like a Champion, UFLI, researchED) show teachers can implement evidence-based practices and see results.
quotes: 54% of U.S. adults read below the equivalent of a sixth-grade level.
Teaching students the fundamentals of literacy using research-backed methods wasn't part of their teacher-training programs.
Newer teachers were likely taught using balanced literacy methods; they can't draw on experience to help students.
Quality PD grounded in evidence allows teachers to put what they learn into practice immediately and witness the difference.
Students can't wait for colleges to change; we need quality PD available to every teacher now.” Archived from Bell Ringers on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
